newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-F.A. REJECTS MIDDLESBROUGH POINTS APPEAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-F.A. REJECTS MIDDLESBROUGH POINTS APPEAL.

text.p: English premier league club Middlesbrough had their appeal against a three-point deduction rejected by the Football Association on Wednesday.
The premier league had imposed the penalty and fined the club 50,000 pounds ($80,000) after they called off their December 20 away fixture at Blackburn because of the unavailability of players.

Middlesbrough, who claimed they would have had to field an under-strength side because 24 players were unavailable through illness, injury and suspension, called off the game without permission from the league 24 hours before the fixture.

The three-man F.A. commission rejected the club's appeal against the deduction and fine and also awarded costs against them. Blackburn's claim that they should be awarded the three points was also rejected.

After a hearing lasting more than five hours the commission announced it was dismissing the appeal after deciding Middlesbrough were quite capable of fielding a team and did not have just cause in cancelling the fixture.
The commission said in a statement that the board accepted Middlesbrough acted in good faith but "considered that the breach of the rules was serious.
"The board does not consider the award of the game to Blackburn as being practical or appropriate," the statement added.

"The board considers that a deduction of three points and a fine of 50,000 pounds is right and fair. The board has ordered Middlesbrough to pay the costs of the premier league and of the board of appeal."

Premier league spokesman Mike Lee said: "We were always confident that the premier league commission had made the right decision and welcome the fact that this has been upheld by the court of appeal."
Middlesbrough manager Bryan Robson said he was "very disappointed by the outcome of the appeal."
Asked if the club were likely to take further action on the case, Robson said: "I have no idea what the policy of the club will be."

Ironically, after the announcement Robson was presented with an award after being named the league's manager of the month for March. The club's Brazilian striker Juninho was also honoured as player of the month.
When the penalty was announced on January 14 Middlesbrough were bottom of the league but a recent good run of results has moved them out of the relegation zone.
On April 6 they will appear in their first major final when they play Leicester in the League Cup decider and a week later face second division Chesterfield in the F.A. Cup semifinals.
